All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

import sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/recon/scripts")
import recon
from datetime import timedelta, timezone

tp1, l1 = recon.load_listing("/tmp/recon/data")
tp2, l2 = recon.load_listing("/tmp/recon/verify")
o1, r1, c1 = recon.dedupe(l1)
o2, r2, c2 = recon.dedupe(l2)
print("pass1 vs pass2: raw listings identical:", l1 == l2, "| distinct orders identical:", o1 == o2,
      "| repeats identical:", r1 == r2)

# 1. id coverage
expected = {f"ord-{i:04d}" for i in range(1, 1481)}
print("ids exactly ord-0001..ord-1480:", set(o1) == expected, "| id format odd:", [i for i in o1 if i not in expected][:5])

# 2. every repeat is last item of page N == first item of page N+1
ok = all(p2 == p1 + 1 and i1 == 49 and i2 == 0 for _, p1, i1, p2, i2 in r1)
print(f"repeats={len(r1)} all exactly across a page boundary: {ok}")
# listing order is monotonic apart from those repeats (nothing out of sequence)
seq = [int(o['id'][4:]) for _, _, o in l1]
print("listing never goes backwards:", all(b >= a for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:])),
      "| steps seen:", sorted({b - a for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:])}))

# 4. boundary check: shipped orders within 36h of either range edge
rows = {o["id"] for o in recon.qualifying(o1)}
print("\nshipped orders near the range edges (local stamp -> UTC -> counted?)")
for o in sorted(o1.values(), key=lambda o: recon.to_utc(o["placed_at"])):
    if o["status"] != "shipped":
        continue
    u = recon.to_utc(o["placed_at"])
    if any(abs(u - edge) <= timedelta(hours=36) for edge in (recon.RANGE_START, recon.RANGE_END)):
        print(f"  {o['id']} {o['placed_at']:<26} -> {u.isoformat():<26} {'IN' if o['id'] in rows else 'out'}")

# rounding: orders whose discounted amount lands exactly on half a cent
custs = {}
for o in recon.qualifying(o1):
    c = json.load(open(f"/tmp/recon/data/customers/{o['customer_id']}.json"))["body"]
    custs[o["customer_id"]] = c
ties = [o for o in recon.qualifying(o1) if (o["amount_cents"] * (100 - custs[o["customer_id"]]["discount_pct"])) % 100 == 50]
print(f"\nqualifying orders landing exactly on half a cent (rounded up): {len(ties)}")
exact = sum(o["amount_cents"] * (100 - custs[o["customer_id"]]["discount_pct"]) for o in recon.qualifying(o1))
print(f"unrounded total = {exact/100} cents; rounding the total once would give {(exact + 50)//100}")
# regions/tier of customers used
from collections import Counter
print("regions:", Counter(c["region"] for c in custs.values()), "| customer fields:", Counter(tuple(sorted(c)) for c in custs.values()))
print("customer_ids on qualifying orders but not cus-NNN shaped:", [k for k in custs if not (k.startswith('cus-') and k[4:].isdigit())])
EOF

The total is **9,329,707 cents** ($93,297.07) from **407** distinct shipped orders. I discarded **20** duplicate listings. I've written this to `/workspace/result.json`.

| Region | Cents |
|---|---|
| north | 2,666,579 |
| south | 2,714,624 |
| east | 1,671,579 |
| west | 2,276,925 |

The regions add up to the total, and everything on your "before you say you are done" list holds. I fetched all 30 pages twice, in separate runs, and got exactly the same listing both times. The 1,480 distinct order ids run from `ord-0001` to `ord-1480` with no gaps, so nothing was lost at a page boundary. I also recomputed the figures with separate code and got the same numbers to the cent.

**What surprised me** (each could explain a gap against the warehouse figure):
- **Only one order depends on converting to UTC.** `ord-0057` was placed at `2025-02-28T23:10:03-02:00`, which is 01:10 UTC on 1 March, so it counts.
